Introduction

Swamiji deserted the academic world to wander aimlessly. He mastered hatha yoga and cultivated psychic powers at the cost (in Dr. Lakhera’s view) of stunting his intellectual growth. But Dr. Lakhera did admit that Swamiji was a remarkable hatha yogi.

In 1983 he asked me to translate his book Living with the Himalayan Masters into Hindi.

You are in the body, yet you are beyond the body. Birth and death are like two commas in the poem of life. For a yogi there is nothing like death. Just as an ordinary person takes off an old tattered garmentand puts on a new one, so does a yogi cast off his worn-outbody and assume a new one.” That is how he himself left his body.

item.title: Tao Te Ching
item.description:
Theme #1 Teachings on non-action

Less and less do you need to force things, until finally you arrive at non-action. When nothing is done, nothing is left undone

There is nothing to be done because it all accumulates to nothing in the very end. If you start to do something, there will always be something more to do. If nothing is done, then there is nothing left to be done as well. This is metaphorical where you need to understand that you wouldn’t have anything to do in this state; not just choosing to not do anything though you want to do it. This is non-action.

item.title: Zen Mind Beginners Mind
item.description:
• Tathagata in Sanskrit and Nyorai in Japanese is a name for Buddha which means “He who has followed the path, who has returned from suchness, or is suchness, thusness, is-ness, emptiness, the fully completed one.”
  • The way of practice in zen is to go from moment to moment doing everything as if you were discovering the thing for the first time. e.g. Calligraphy without trying to make something skillful or beautiful.
  • Pondering over koans, why a master would say such things, are not obvious at first but illuminating later on when they are read carefully.
  • Teacher’s utter ordinariness intrigues student about the whole nature. A student learns by seeing through teacher’s actions. It often happens that student is moved by the simplicity rather than anything extraordinary.
  • Beginner’s mind means ready for everything that comes through.
  • Try to maintain right posture throughout day to day activities as well.
  • We only do anything as it comes during zazen.
  • We practice zazen with the understanding that all things are quiet independent, but yet dependent. We shouldn’t be bothered by anything else as we practice zazen just like mountains aren’t bothered by clouds.
  • We perceive beauty when things get out of balance against a background of perfect balance.
  • The best way to control people is to encourage them to be mischievous, similar to how you can control your sheep/cow by giving them a large enough meadow.
    • First let people do what they want, and watch them. To ignore is the worst policy. Second worst is trying to control them.
  • Concentrating your mind on anything is not true purpose of Zen.
  • In zazen, there are no waves. No effort required to do zazen. By practicing zazen, the waves become smaller and smaller, thus changing any effort into some subtle feeling.
  • Waves during zazen are like weeds which we give to our meditation to bring nourishment to our process by watching them, thus burying them while making zazen better.
  • So, it’s necessary to make effort until the moment when effort disappears. This place is not attained by action of effort, but by just putting in effort without fixating on the point where effort disappears.
  • We all want to be the best pupil where we learn the truth without any external whip, but even if we can’t; we can do it with shadow of a whip before it hits us. That’s better than actually getting whipped badly to learn.
    • But there is so much contradiction in Zen. The one that finds it easy to sit physically usually takes more time to get to the true way. Then, our best becomes worst, and vice versa.
    • Conclusion: You learn, but there’s no right or wrong, fast or slow. Just do it, and let the waves flow you. You just practice.
  • Sit without any ideas, any expectations. Don’t even take the idea of emptiness and form while doing so based on “Prajna Paramita Sutra”.
  • Saying everything is a practice for zazen even when you lie down without realizing the true understanding of it is just you being lazy. When you will have understood, there is no need to practice zazen at all. If you still need to practice, practice it in a posture. Know when your small mind makes excuses.
  • For beginner, practice without effort is not true practice. Practice needs great effort till the point you forget all about yourself.
  • Bowing is a practice to eliminate our self-centered ideas.
  • Calmness in activity is true calmness.
  • There is no need to worry about progress. You just watch in zazen as guided. There is no purpose of zazen. It’s just there to show you what you already are, what you already have.
  • It’s more about letting the river flow on original path by letting other forces that are changing it’s path come to a halt.
  • Bodhisattva’s way is like one railway track thousands of miles long. But a bodhisattva has no idea of tracks, only the views from the train. No need for passengers to be curious about the track.
  • Zen isn’t something to be curious about. Don’t be too interested in the idea itself.
  • Don’t put special effort to achieve something, some excessive quality, some extra element’s involvement. Make it simple. e.g. When you practice well, you have pride which is extra. You need to get rid of anything that’s extra.
  • By not fixating on anything, and realizing that zazen is already there, nothing can escape the sight. Nothing can escape because nothing is being fixated on.
  • Thinking creeps into actions making our mental contents more complex.
    • Right thinking doesn’t leave any traces or shadow on our mind. Of course, it’s necessary to think or prepare before we act.
    • To leave a trace is not the same as remembering something. It’s attachment to traces of thought and activity.
    • To not leave traces, you need to do it with complete body and mind in action. Like a good bonfire, it burns everything once it completes.
  • “Dana Prajna Paramita”. Dogen-zenzi said “To give is non-attachment.”
  • Zazen is not done for the sake of joy in it. Finding joy in there isn’t very good either.
  • There is no way: you need to find the kind of practice you have right now, and also your way.
  • Being concentrated in what you are doing at the moment is one way to not focus on some goal. This is “ichigjo-zammai” or one-act samadhi.
  • You need a teacher to become independent.
  • Encouragement is like medicine. We need it when we are sick, but it’s not food. Mistaking it for food can happen easily.
  • When you eat, you eat. When you walk, you walk. Without any worry, do what you are doing at the moment.
  • The more you know about Zen, the more your mind becomes filled with rubbish. Quiet contradictory because knowledge isn’t experience. The more the contents in your mind, the lesser you are in the moment itself. So, right orientation is necessary when gathering knowledge.
    • Once you start to understand, everything you hear will feel more and more like what you already knew.
  • To understand it all, you need patience without effort of being patient.
  • Express without intention and you just let emotions be without any attachment.
  • Zazen is Hinayana practice with Mahayana spirit - rigid formal practice with informal mind.
  • Trying to win the discussion is the wrong attitude. Try not to either win nor lose.
  • Trying to understand what Zen masters do, and imitate is never a good idea. There are things masters do, and it’s from their mode of understanding. You don’t try to rationalize what Zen master did.
  • Talking about zen is easy, but to have this actual feeling isn’t so easy. You miss it out very easily.
  • The harmony of calmness and activity is the quality of being.
  • Before you do anything, being is there, result is there. The result of your sitting is already there. All the activity is included within you.
  • You are like the seed who doesn’t know about the plant it’s going to become, but is in perfect harmony with the ground as well as it’s surroundings.
  • Any activity that comes out of nothingness is natural. “Shin ku myo u” ( From true emptiness, the wondrous being appears ).
  • “Nyu nan shin” ( Smooth, natural mind )
  • Hopes or any idea about the future moves us away from this moment.
  • Concentration means freedom. Your effort should be directed at nothing. Even when zazen asks to concentrate your mind on breathing is to forget all about yourself and just sit and feel yourself breathing.
  • Bodhidharma’s zazen is that even before we practice it, enlightenment is there.
  • Our mind should be soft and open enough to understand things as they are.
  • If we are prepared for thinking, there is no need to make an effort to think. This is mindfulness, at the same time, wisdom.
  • There is not even emphasis on oneness. If it is one, there is no need to emphasize one. So, accepting it is not the usual way of accepting. It happens. It’s not done.
  • You do zazen even when you don’t find anything or you just find weeds, trees, or clouds in your daily life.
  • Physical as well as mental calmness by sitting straight without leaning over or against something.
  • When effort arises from pure origin, all you do will be good, and you’ll be satisfied with anything you do.

How to meditate (Zazen)

  • Sitting in lotus position has nothing magical to it. It’s to make legs feel like one: thus expressing oneness of duality. You don’t know which is left one and which is right one.
  • Relax your shoulders and push up towards the ceiling with the back of your head.
  • To gain strength in your posture:
    • Pull your chin in so that you have strength in your posture; thus preventing you from falling asleep.
    • Press diaphgram down towards lower abdomen.
      • NOTE:: Breating might feel a little difficult at first but it’s okay.
  • Hands in cosmic mudra
    • Left on top of right
    • Middle joints of your middle fingers together.
    • Touch thumbs lightly as if there’s a paper between them thus making an oval.
  • Keep mudra as if you are holding something with great care.
  • Hands held against the body with thumbs at about the height of your navel.
  • Arms free and easy, slightly away from your body as if you held an egg under each arm without breaking it.

Quotes

When we have no thought of achievement, no thought of self, we are true beginners. Then we can really learn something. The beginner’s mind is the mind of compassion.
